method: Read the petdex submission tracker rather than the star count: the open issues are ordinary people uploading their own drawn creatures (one titled 「[Submit fail] 宇智波佐助」) and a rights-holder asking for two entries to be withdrawn. Volume of user-drawn art plus an IP dispute, four months in, is behaviour evidence that the drawing half of this is already happening. Then checked the radar index — 桌宠 appears zero times across 567 entries.
gap: Only geeks can see it. The capability, the art pipeline and the audience sit in three different places: the pets live in a terminal, the people who want a companion on screen are on ordinary Windows and macOS desktops, and the newest piece — turning one hand-drawn picture into a full animated spritesheet — is wired to neither.

zh.gap: 只有极客能看见它。能力、美术管线和人群分在三个地方：宠物住在终端里，想要屏幕上有个同伴的人在普通 Windows 和 macOS 桌面上，而最新的那一环——把一张手绘图变成整套动画序列——两边都没接上。
zh.pain: 人们已经在画像素小生物、成百上百地上传了——而唯一能放它的地方是一个终端窗口，他家孩子、他妈、以及任何他想拿去炫的人，都永远不会打开那东西。
zh.kill: 桌宠免费了十五年，为它收钱这件事从未被验证过，天花板可能干脆是零。它是半衰期很短的新奇：笑点过了就关掉，没有第二天回来的理由。更糟的是，「画→动画序列」这一步就是整个产品，而它恰恰最容易出错——把孩子的怪物画歪一点，不是可爱，是让孩子难过。
zh.move: 交付管线，不是图鉴：拍一张画，当分钟就得到一只在桌面上走的同伴；而给它第二天的理由是——让它对这台机器真正知道的那一件事有反应，比如电脑闲着的时候它就睡觉。永远不做交易市集，永远不放别人的生物。冷启动（中文）：小红书／B站「桌宠」「孩子画的怪物」评论区，以及儿童画账号下面排队的那批人；（英文）：r/desktoppets 与 r/Unity3D 的业余圈，加上这个项目自己的提交队列——那里已经全是普通人在上传自己画的生物。
zh.hook: 今天下午孩子画了一只怪物，问能不能让它住进电脑里的那个人。已经有好几百人在手工画这些东西并往一个项目里提交，而那个项目唯一的显示界面是一个终端窗口。
zh.does: 一堆住在你机器里的像素小生物。切口是：把一张手绘图变成一只在普通 Windows／macOS 桌面上走动的动画同伴。
zh.consumer_angle: 一个家长和一个孩子，看着孩子今天下午画的那只东西在家里的笔记本上走过去。不用终端，不用编译。

pain: People are already drawing sprite creatures and uploading them by the hundred — and the only place to put one is a terminal window that their kid, their mum and everyone else they would show it to will never open.
kill: Desktop pets have been free for fifteen years, so charging for one is unproven and the ceiling may be zero. It is novelty with a short half-life: the joke fades, the pet gets closed, and there is nothing to come back for. Worse, the drawing-to-spritesheet step is the whole product and it is the part most likely to look wrong — a child's creature rendered slightly off is not charming, it is upsetting to the child.
move: Ship the pipeline, not the collection: photograph one drawing, get back an animated companion that walks on the desktop the same minute, and — the part that gives it a second day — it reacts to the one thing that machine actually knows, e.g. it naps when the laptop is idle. Never a marketplace, never other people's creatures. Cold start (Chinese): 小红书/B站 「桌宠」「孩子画的怪物」 comment sections, and the queues under 儿童画 accounts; (English): r/desktoppets and the r/Unity3D hobby crowd, plus the submission tracker on the project itself, which is already full of ordinary people uploading their own drawn creatures.
hook: The person whose kid drew a creature this afternoon and asked whether it could live in the computer. Hundreds of people are already drawing and submitting these by hand into a project whose only display surface is a terminal window.
does: A collection of sprite creatures that live on your machine. The wedge: turn one hand-drawn picture into an animated companion that walks around an ordinary Windows or macOS desktop.
consumer_angle: A parent and a child watch the thing the child drew this afternoon walk across the family laptop. No terminal, no build step.
